proposition: The papers differ on who led whom between Ibn Turka and Iskandar. Timurid-Mughal says Iskandar embraced lettrism at Ibn Turka's instance; New Brethren says Ibn Turka's key works were almost certainly commissioned by Iskandar; Selenocentrism calls Ibn Turka 'Iskandar's inspiration' and offers Iamblichus and Julian as the model; the dissertation says Iskandar was himself an imamophile with a pronounced interest in lettrism and may be imagined as taking warmly to Ibn Turka.
